---
title: Evals
description: Manage benchmarks and their cases, then run them against your agents on managed Sessions — Harbor-format tasks such as Terminal-Bench, or scripted conversations.
---

import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Evals have three layers:

- **Benchmark** — a named set of cases. Each benchmark has one kind:
  - **`harbor`** — cases are tasks in the [Harbor](https://harborframework.com)
    task format (`task.toml`, `instruction.md`, `environment/`, `tests/`,
    `solution/`). This is the format Terminal-Bench 2.0 uses.
  - **`messages`** — cases are scripted conversations: user messages sent in
    order, then an eval-core reward spec scores the Session.
- **Case** — one task of a benchmark. Harbor cases are read-only in OMA: you
  edit them where they live (a git repository, a Hugging Face dataset, your own
  directory) and sync the benchmark. Messages cases are edited in OMA.
- **Eval run** — one execution of a benchmark (all cases or some of them)
  against an agent. Every attempt (a **trial**) is an ordinary managed Session,
  so you can open it in the Console and read exactly what the agent did. A
  background tick drives runs forward once a minute on both Node and
  Cloudflare deployments.

A Harbor run is bound to the benchmark revision that was current when it
started and reads every case by its content digest; a messages run keeps a copy
of its cases. Syncing or editing later never changes a run. A benchmark cannot
be deleted while one of its runs is pending or running (`409`).

## Harbor benchmarks

### Import

```bash
# A git repository: github.com or a Hugging Face dataset. --ref is a branch,
# tag or commit (default: the default branch); --path imports one folder of
# tasks (or one task). `oma evals benchmarks refs <url>` lists the branches and tags.
oma evals benchmarks refs https://github.com/laude-institute/terminal-bench-2
oma evals benchmarks import --git https://github.com/laude-institute/terminal-bench-2 --ref main
oma evals benchmarks import --git https://huggingface.co/datasets/harborframework/harbor-datasets \
  --path datasets/bird-bench --case california_schools__13

# Any dataset in Harbor's public registry (or --registry-url for your own)
oma evals benchmarks import --registry terminal-bench@2.0 --case fix-git --case regex-log

# A benchmark shipped with OMA (pinned to a commit)
oma evals benchmarks import --builtin terminal-bench-sample@2.0

# Your own tasks: a directory or a .tar / .tar.gz containing task directories
oma evals benchmarks upload ./my-tasks --name my-tasks
```

In the console, the import and sync dialogs list the repository's branches and
tags (default branch preselected) and also accept any typed ref or commit sha.

An import resolves the ref to a commit, reads the task directories at that
commit and stores them as **revision 1**. `oma evals benchmarks show <id>`
lists the source, the pinned commits, the revisions and each case with its
digest and whether it can run on this deployment.

Git sources other than github.com and huggingface.co, and Harbor Hub packages,
are not supported yet and are rejected with an explicit error. Hub datasets are
read file by file; import large ones in subsets with `--case`.

### Change cases: edit at the source, then sync

```bash
oma evals benchmarks sync <benchmark-id>                  # re-resolve the ref, re-read the tasks
oma evals benchmarks sync <benchmark-id> --ref v2         # git: move to another branch, tag or commit
oma evals benchmarks sync <benchmark-id> --file ./my-tasks # upload: a new directory or archive
oma evals benchmarks show <benchmark-id> --revision 1     # an older revision
oma evals cases show <benchmark-id> fix-git --revision 1
```

A sync makes a new revision only when the content changed, as `harbor
publish` does: each case's digest is Harbor's package hash
(sha256 over sorted `path\0sha256(file)\n` lines) over the files OMA stores —
`task.toml`, `instruction.md`, `tests/`, `solution/`. `environment/` is not
stored, because cases run from their prebuilt image, so the digest is not the
same as a Harbor Hub digest of the task. A sync that finds the same content
writes nothing. Revisions are never changed afterwards.

### How a trial runs

1. The case's container image is the Session's sandbox. The working directory
   is the image's `WORKDIR`, exactly as Harbor runs it.
2. **Agent mode**: `instruction.md` is sent as the first user message and the
   agent works until it ends its turn. If it exceeds the task's agent timeout
   it is interrupted and the trial is still graded.
   **Oracle mode**: `solution/solve.sh` runs instead of an agent. Use it to
   check that a case's environment and tests work here before spending model
   tokens.
3. `tests/` is copied into the same sandbox and `tests/test.sh` runs. It
   writes `/logs/verifier/reward.txt` or `reward.json`; that is the trial's
   reward.

A case passes when its reward is at least 1. A case's mean reward counts
errored trials as 0, as Harbor does; the run score is the mean over cases.

### Task images

Harbor tasks name a prebuilt image (`docker_image` in `task.toml`). OMA only
runs images the operator has listed in `SANDBOX_IMAGES`; a case whose image is
not listed is shown as not runnable and is rejected when you start a run.
`SANDBOX_IMAGES` is described in `docs/self-host.md` in the repository; on
Cloudflare each image is built into its own container class, see
`docs/cloudflare-sandbox-images.md`.

<Aside type="caution">
Tasks that build their image from a Dockerfile, use docker-compose services or
restrict networking are not supported yet and are rejected with an explicit
error.
</Aside>

## Messages benchmarks

A messages case sends its messages one at a time, waiting for the agent to
finish each turn, then scores the Session's trajectory. Write a case as JSON:

```json
{
  "name": "two-turns",
  "messages": ["Write first to /tmp/a.txt", "Print /tmp/a.txt"],
  "reward": { "type": "verifiable", "scorer": "agentMessageContains", "opts": { "target": "first" } }
}
```

```bash
oma evals benchmarks create --name smoke --kind messages
oma evals cases add <benchmark-id> --file two-turns.json
oma evals cases replace <benchmark-id> two-turns --file two-turns.json
```

`reward.type` is one of `verifiable`, `script`, `reward_model` or
`composite`. Optional `setup_files` and `setup_script` prepare the sandbox
before the first message; `timeout_ms` bounds the case. Messages runs use the
environment you pass when starting the run; on Cloudflare it must be a cloud
environment.

## Run a benchmark

```bash
# Harbor: check the environments first, then the agent
oma evals run --benchmark <benchmark-id> --mode oracle --wait
oma evals run --benchmark <benchmark-id> --agent <agent-id> --trials 2 --concurrency 4 --wait

# Messages: an agent and an environment
oma evals run --benchmark <benchmark-id> --agent <agent-id> --environment <env-id> --wait

oma evals runs list --benchmark <benchmark-id>
oma evals runs show <run-id>
oma evals runs cancel <run-id>
```

`--case` (repeatable) runs a subset. `--concurrency` caps how many trials run
at once (default 4).

The same operations are in the Console under **Evals** (tabs **Benchmarks** and
**Runs**), and in the SDK:

```ts
const evals = client.oma.evals;

// Harbor: import, then run
const tb = await evals.benchmarks.create({
  source: { type: "builtin", name: "terminal-bench-sample@2.0" },
});
const { run_id } = await evals.runs.create({
  benchmark_id: tb.id, agent_id: "agent_123", trials: 2,
});
console.log((await evals.runs.waitForRun(run_id)).score);

// Messages: create, add a case, run
const smoke = await evals.benchmarks.create({ kind: "messages", name: "smoke" });
await evals.benchmarks.cases.add(smoke.id, {
  name: "two-turns",
  messages: ["Write first to /tmp/a.txt", "Print /tmp/a.txt"],
  reward: { type: "verifiable", scorer: "agentMessageContains", opts: { target: "first" } },
});
await evals.runs.create({ benchmark_id: smoke.id, agent_id: "agent_123", environment_id: "env_123" });
```

### Inline messages runs

The original API still accepts tasks inline, without a benchmark:

```bash
curl -X POST $OMA/v1/oma/evals/runs \
  -H "x-api-key: $KEY" -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "agent_id": "agent_123",
    "environment_id": "env_123",
    "tasks": [{
      "id": "two-turns",
      "messages": ["Write first to /tmp/a.txt", "Print /tmp/a.txt"],
      "reward": { "type": "verifiable", "scorer": "agentMessageContains", "opts": { "target": "first" } }
    }]
  }'
```

## Limits

- On Node, sandboxes live in the control-plane process: restarting it fails the
  trials that were running.
- On Cloudflare, an exec returns at most 100 KB of output and an idle container
  sleeps after 5 minutes.
